about.heading: WHO IS BEHIND THE SYSTEM?
about.intro: I'm Tejas Jagdale, a backend developer focused on building reliable APIs, AI-powered systems, and scalable backend infrastructure.
bio: Operating at the intersection of robust backend engineering and applied artificial intelligence, I engineer systems that are both deterministic and capable of autonomous reasoning.

My work centers on designing event-driven microservices, implementing high-throughput asynchronous pipelines, orchestrating multi-agent LLM workflows with LangGraph, and deploying resilient infrastructure on AWS and Docker.

I treat software engineering as a craft of precision: minimizing p99 latencies, ensuring fault tolerance across distributed boundaries, and delivering clean, observable systems that scale cleanly under production pressure.

projects.name: InfraMind
projects.description: An autonomous AI orchestration engine that monitors distributed backend microservices, detects anomalies in real-time, and executes self-healing remediation routines through verified LangGraph multi-agent state graphs.
projects.problem: Modern distributed microservices generate overwhelming operational telemetry. Traditional alerting triggers static thresholds that often page on-call engineers without root-cause diagnosis or actionable remediation.
projects.solution: InfraMind ingests operational logs and telemetry through an async FastAPI gateway, coordinates an autonomous multi-agent hierarchy (Anomaly Detector -> Root Cause Planner -> Tool Executor -> Verifier) via LangGraph, and resolves operational incidents within sandboxed boundaries.

projects.name: VectorFlow-RAG
projects.description: Production-grade retrieval augmented generation pipeline combining dense embeddings with BM25 sparse search and cross-encoder re-ranking for enterprise documentation.
projects.problem: Standard vector similarity search frequently fails on exact keyword identifiers, version codes, and technical jargon, causing hallucinated answers.
projects.solution: Engineered a two-stage hybrid retrieval architecture blending ChromaDB dense vector lookups with BM25 full-text indexing, followed by a BGE cross-encoder re-ranking stage.
implementation: Recursive text chunking with semantic markdown awareness and metadata preservation.
Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) algorithm to balance keyword and semantic score distributions.
Asynchronous batch embedding generation with local rate-limit token bucket queues.
challenges: Balancing retrieval recall against latency constraints in real-time query scenarios.
results: Achieved a 38% improvement in retrieval precision over naive vector-only semantic search.
Maintained sub-80ms retrieval and re-ranking time for document corpuses of 100k+ tokens.

projects.name: RedNet
projects.description: A lightweight distributed in-memory data store supporting Redis protocol wire compatibility, master-replica asynchronous replication, and pub/sub message brokering.
projects.problem: Understanding distributed storage internals requires building from first principles rather than treating Redis as a black box.
projects.solution: Built a non-blocking asynchronous event loop server supporting RESP (Redis Serialization Protocol), in-memory hash indexing, key expiration with active sampling, and snapshotting.
implementation: Custom byte-level parser for RESP protocol tokens handling pipelined client requests.
Sliding expiration manager combining passive expiration on access with probabilistic periodic sweeps.
Non-blocking append-only log (AOF) persistence engine ensuring durability.
challenges: Minimizing memory fragmentation while handling rapid key churn and high-frequency writes.
results: Benchmark sustained 45,000+ operations/second on a single modern CPU core with minimal overhead.

projects.name: AuthX
projects.description: Zero-trust authentication and authorization microservice featuring asymmetric JWT signing, automated token rotation, fine-grained RBAC, and sliding-window rate limiting.
projects.problem: Decentralized microservice architectures need rapid token verification without hitting the primary authentication database on every internal request.
projects.solution: Created an RS256 asymmetric public-key identity microservice with Redis token revocation blacklists and sliding window rate limiting.
implementation: Public/private keypair rotation allowing downstream microservices to verify tokens locally with cached public keys.
Redis sorted set (ZSET) implementation of rolling sliding-window request throttling.
Password hashing using Argon2id with adaptive memory and parallelism costs.
challenges: Ensuring instant global revocation of compromised refresh tokens across distributed microservices.
results: Local token verification overhead under 0.8ms; handles 10,000+ authentication handshakes per minute.

projects.name: MarketPulse AI
projects.description: Multi-agent research and sentiment analysis engine that aggregates SEC filings, market news, and quantitative pricing signals to synthesize unbiased equity research dossiers.
projects.problem: Analyzing unstructured market disclosures across hundreds of companies requires tedious manual collation prone to cognitive biases.
projects.solution: Employed a committee of specialized agents: Quantitative Analyst, Fundamental Reader, and Devil's Advocate Critic that debate evidence before compiling findings.
implementation: Multi-agent debate loop where the Critic agent challenges unverified bullish/bearish claims.
Dynamic tool calling to Yahoo Finance, SEC EDGAR APIs, and news vector indexes.
Structured Markdown synthesis with source citations and confidence scores.
challenges: Preventing agents from getting trapped in endless debate cycles using token budget dampeners.
results: Reduced equity disclosure research time from 4 hours to under 3 minutes per quarterly report.

projects.name: FastPik
projects.description: High-throughput asynchronous media ingestion service that processes image transforms, video transcoding, and automated thumbnail extraction using Celery and S3.
projects.problem: Heavy image and video transcoding blocks web server worker threads and leads to request timeouts.
projects.solution: Built an asynchronous presigned S3 upload architecture with decoupled Celery workers, Redis queues, and webhook completion notifications.
implementation: Direct-to-S3 client uploads via pre-signed URLs to bypass API server bandwidth bottlenecks.
Celery task priority queues dividing quick thumbnail generation from long-running transcode jobs.
Automatic retry logic with exponential backoff on transient AWS network failures.
challenges: Handling sudden spikes of 100+ concurrent multi-megabyte media uploads without memory exhaustion.
results: Zero API server worker thread blockage; processed 500GB+ of media files with 100% completion rate.

projects.name: HexaLink
projects.description: Ultra-low latency URL redirection system using Base62 encoding, Redis Bloom filters for rapid existence checks, and PostgreSQL read replicas.
projects.problem: High-volume URL redirection services must respond in single-digit milliseconds and handle cache misses without saturating database connections.
projects.solution: Integrated Redis Bloom filters to detect non-existent short keys in <1ms before touching cache or disk, paired with LRU hot-key caching.
implementation: Distributed ID generator using Snowflake-inspired 64-bit integer scheme encoded to Base62.
Redis Bloom filter layer with 0.1% false positive probability to intercept malicious cache-miss probing.
Asynchronous click analytics buffering in Redis lists before batch ingestion to PostgreSQL.
challenges: Eliminating cache stampedes on viral URLs using mutex lock leasing.
results: Sub-12ms p99 redirect latency under 15,000 synthetic requests/second.

aiWorkflow.heading: I BUILD AI SYSTEMS THAT ACT.
aiWorkflow.subheading: Deterministic execution graphs orchestrating autonomous reasoning, tool validation, and state persistence.
aiWorkflow.description: Moving beyond naive chat interfaces into production-grade agentic architectures. In my systems, AI models don't just generate text; they formulate plans, interact with real APIs, query knowledge bases, validate outputs against strict schemas, and correct their own errors.

steps.title: USER INTENT
steps.label: USER
steps.desc: Receives raw request from developer, API client, or operational trigger with context and constraints.
steps.details: Input is sanitized, tagged with session credentials, and parsed for required parameter boundaries before admission into the execution graph.

steps.title: INTENT EXTRACTION
steps.label: INTENT
steps.desc: Extracts semantic entities, operation objectives, and environmental constraints using structured output schemas.
steps.details: Converts ambiguous natural language or alert payloads into strict Pydantic models containing actionable goal primitives.

steps.title: PLANNER ENGINE
steps.label: PLANNER
steps.desc: Formulates a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) of sub-tasks, establishing dependencies and validation checkpoints.
steps.details: Leverages LangGraph state nodes to determine whether immediate tool invocation, knowledge retrieval, or multi-agent delegation is required.

steps.title: KNOWLEDGE RETRIEVAL
steps.label: RESEARCH
steps.desc: Queries vector stores, operational logs, and live system state to ground decisions with factual context.
steps.details: Executes hybrid BM25 + dense embedding lookups across ChromaDB/Pinecone to supply relevant documentation without context window bloat.

steps.title: TOOL EXECUTION
steps.label: TOOLS
steps.desc: Executes concrete functions: database queries, HTTP requests, shell commands, or service restarts.
steps.details: Tools run inside isolated execution environments with strict permission scopes, timeout limits, and failure fallback handlers.

steps.title: STATE & MEMORY
steps.label: MEMORY
steps.desc: Stores intermediate execution state, agent scratchpads, and execution history into Redis and PostgreSQL.
steps.details: Enables pause-and-resume workflows, human-in-the-loop approvals, and complete state rollbacks in case of unexpected failure.

steps.title: OUTPUT VALIDATION
steps.label: VALIDATION
steps.desc: Rigorous verification against expected Pydantic models, safety policies, and unit assertions.
steps.details: If validation fails, the error feedback is injected directly back into the Planner node for autonomous self-correction cycles.

steps.title: PRODUCTION RESULT
steps.label: RESULT
steps.desc: Delivers deterministic, structured response payload to the caller with full execution trace and audit logs.
steps.details: Emits telemetry metrics to monitoring dashboards and commits the completed incident or response transaction.
